requirements.title: Direct access accesses external record-file records in arbitrary order
requirements.definition: Direct access is a method of accessing records of an external record file in arbitrary order.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

Access-position fixture implementation: 1 valid run-phase scratch-file program(s) cover `direct-access-arbitrary-record-order`. They create the external files in the run directory with STATUS='SCRATCH' and also close with STATUS='DELETE'. Oracles are limited to exact integer/character values, character lengths, IOSTAT zero, IOSTAT_END, and POS= inequalities or values fixed by this source. No file name, external representation, processor-specific IOSTAT number, IOMSG text, formatted-stream byte spacing, or unsupported cross-access-method property is asserted.

requirements.title: Direct records are identified by immutable positive record numbers and ordered by those numbers
requirements.definition: Each direct-access record is uniquely identified by a positive integer record number specified when written; once established, the record number cannot be changed, and record order is record-number order.

pending.direct-record-order-number-order: If later sequential view is supported, verify sequential order follows record numbers; otherwise retain as source-use property without physical-order oracle.

requirements.title: Direct files have uniform record form and constrained endfile treatment
requirements.definition: Direct-file records are either all formatted or all unformatted; if sequential access is also allowed, any endfile record is not part of the file while connected for direct access; if sequential access is not allowed, the file shall not contain an endfile record.

pending.direct-records-all-formatted-or-all-unfo: Positive controls use separate formatted and unformatted direct files; no mixed-form diagnostic is claimed here.
pending.direct-endfile-ignored-when-sequential-a: No portable oracle exists without a processor profile supporting both access methods and an observable endfile transition; future tests must not inspect hidden endfile representation.
pending.direct-endfile-prohibited-without-sequen: Negative source-control only; setup must first establish no sequential access for that file, which is processor dependent.

requirements.title: Direct-file records are read or written only by direct access data transfer statements
requirements.definition: The records of a direct file shall be read or written only by direct access data transfer statements.

pending.direct-records-direct-transfer-only: Positive plan uses direct READ/WRITE with REC=. A negative source-control attempts sequential transfer on the same direct connection, but diagnostic observation belongs to data-transfer rules.

requirements.definition: All records of a direct-access file have the same length.

requirements.title: Direct records may be read or written out of record-number order subject to write/read permission conditions
requirements.definition: Direct records need not be read or written in record-number order; any record may be written while connected; any written record may be read while connected if READ is permitted for the connection.

requirements.title: Direct files shall not use list-directed, namelist, or nonadvancing data transfer
requirements.definition: Direct-file records shall not be read or written using list-directed formatting, namelist formatting, or a nonadvancing data transfer statement.

pending.direct-list-directed-prohibited: Negative source-control uses a direct connection and list-directed transfer, with a formatted-direct control differing only by explicit format; portable diagnostic attribution is deferred to data-transfer rules.
pending.direct-namelist-prohibited: Negative source-control uses direct connection and NML=, with a sequential namelist control; no IOMSG wording or status number asserted.
pending.direct-nonadvancing-prohibited: Negative source-control uses ADVANCE= on direct connection, with sequential nonadvancing control after 12.3.4.2; attribution must reach this prohibition.

accounting.rationale: Direct-access properties mix definitions, permissions, and several distinct prohibitions.
Permits out-of-order/gap writes and reads of written records.
Three distinct prohibitions for direct files.
NOTE explains that records cannot be deleted but can be rewritten; it is not a normative basis here.
